score_meanings.promise_vocabulary: 0 drifts into claims/profiles/central trust-ledger framing, 5 stays promise-first and pCID-specific
score_meanings.simplicity_durability: 0 overbuilt or fragile, 5 minimal, durable, and small-device-friendly under the 100-year goal

promise_theory_rules: A promise is a scoped declaration of intent.
No agent can make a promise on behalf of another agent.
Trust is a local assessment of whether a promise will be kept.
Promises to receive or use are not equivalent to obligations, impositions, or promises to give.
promise_theory_references: Mark Burgess, In Search of Certainty
Mark Burgess, Promise Theory: Principles and Applications

assessment.rationale: Good match on immutable audit evidence and safe evolution after freeze: concrete CAS citations and peer-local records help prevent silent history mutation. But the simulation does not fully specify freeze lineage semantics for whether a breaking post-freeze change becomes a new specimen, a superseding identifier, or an amendment, and its language leans more toward conformance claims than explicit agent promises.
strengths: Strong durable citation discipline for frozen evidence.
Clear separation of local, live, audit, and effect layers.
Peer-local records improve long-term auditability and dispute handling.
Supports evolution without mutating prior cited objects.
weaknesses: Does not define a concrete supersession/amendment mechanism for frozen group-session artifacts.
Promise vocabulary is weaker than ideal PT wording.
risks: Post-freeze lineage may remain ambiguous across embodiments.
Conformance-manifest framing may invite overclaiming beyond what one agent actually promises.
The bundle/manifest pattern is somewhat heavier than minimal durable artifacts.
open_questions: How should a post-freeze breaking change be represented explicitly: new specimen, superseding contract-family reference, or amendment object?
What durable lineage object links old frozen audit evidence to the new mutation request without implying history rewrite?
How should per-agent manifests state supersession so Carol can distinguish coexistence from replacement?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.

autonomous_agents.note: Each peer publishes its own scoped manifest and keeps its own promise-accounting records.

no_promises_for_others.note: Mostly local, but app-level conformance manifest language can be read as speaking for a broader app or embodiment set unless explicitly recast as per-agent promises.

no_guaranteed_outcomes.note: The design distinguishes identity, availability, authorization, and effect, and records failed or unknown outcomes.

local_trust_assessment.note: Trust is grounded in peer-local records and cited CAS artifacts rather than a global registry.

accept_use_not_obligation.note: Peers can inspect cited artifacts locally; publication does not by itself impose acceptance or use.

violations: Uses conformance-manifest/claim framing instead of consistently promise-first wording.
'Authoritative' app-level contract references risk sounding global unless kept strictly as a cited boundary object for local promises.
